executiveSummary: GM0590 passes the complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract. Its CBS/PDOK 2025 identity, 32,299-person municipality control, 34 neighbourhoods in nine districts, one BAG place and three BRT settlements are coherent; neighbourhood rows sum to 32,280, only 19 below the separately published control (-0.059%). Release is nevertheless correction-required. Papendrecht is a dense dike-town in dike ring 16 at the Noord–Beneden-Merwede confluence, with distinct binnendijkse polder/singel/sewer/pump and buitendijkse harbour/Oosteind industrial pathways. A bounded LIWO query returns two primary candidates and zero regional candidates; the Noord km 977.7 point is contained, while Beneden Merwede km 971.4 lies just outside the generalized boundary. Yet the river preset reports exactly 3.365328 m from T+12 through T+72, 15,745 affected at T+24 and 1,283,168.417 deprived person-hours at T+72 without selecting either hydraulic case, water level/datum, dike/structure state, footprint, arrival or recession. Pluvial reports 0.773943 m and Drainage availability 0.414381 at T+24 without Papendrecht's stress-test/WRP, sewer, singel, groundwater, pump or receiving-river state, then clears exactly by T+72. Storm, pluvial, river, heat, cyber, wildfire/smoke and compound reuse the same resident-heavy top-five ranking and omit the explicit binnendijks/buitendijks split; Bedrijventerrein Oosteind en Ketel has 25 residents but 220 businesses and 221 non-residential buildings. Current access is materially contradicted: official municipal evidence says the N3 Papendrecht bridge is fully closed to road traffic for nine months from 17 July 2026, the Baanhoek cycle route is restricted, and two temporary passenger ferries operate, while the model continues to assign the N3 edge 150 scenario units. A15 has three logical municipal edges on one physical corridor, and no rail station or event-time waterbus/bus/external-care route is modeled. Public context contains fourteen partial water/wastewater assets, one Stedin planning sample with null existing/required values, 54 antenna sites and 21 education locations; no internal RIVM acute-care respondent, Waterinfo observation/forecast or NDW situation is assigned. Unknown, NoData, candidate catalogues, plans, registers and recurring schedules must never become zero, safe, open or operational.

evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0590 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place, settlement and safety-region context
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated snapshots retrieved 31 August–2 September 2026
supports: Annual CBS/PDOK inputs identify GM0590 as Papendrecht in Zuid-Holland and safety region Zuid-Holland-Zuid and report 32,299 residents, density 3,431/km², 23.2% aged 65 or older and 4,775 one-person households; the generated centre [4.706362758024193,51.83224062409831] lies inside the boundary.

Thirty-four neighbourhood rows in nine districts sum to 32,280 residents, 19 below the separately published municipality control (-0.059%); households sum to 14,305 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 7,500. Allocation reconciles to the control without rewriting source rows.
BAG supplies one place, Papendrecht. BRT supplies Papendrecht, Matena and Oosteind as one woonkern and two deelkernen; no BAG centre lies outside the generalized boundary.

All 36 CBS fields are exposed. District heating and charging are null in all 34 rows; eleven rows lack multiple housing/benefit/car fields and nine lack several density/distance fields. Null/suppression remains NoData. CBS/PDOK is CC BY 4.0 and BAG is Public Domain Mark 1.0.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Strategy Climate Adaptation Papendrecht and Water- en Rioleringsprogramma 2025–2029
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal adaptation strategy and WRP 2025–2029 public council package inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The strategy describes Papendrecht as a Merwede dike-town kept dry by sewers, singels, dikes and pumps, and explicitly separates binnendijkse and buitendijkse areas. The harbour, Oosteind industry and some homes are outside the dike, where river level directly affects business activity.

The binnendijkse system comprises ditches and singels; municipal evidence separately discusses intense rainfall, groundwater nuisance, heat and drought. The 2025–2029 WRP at https://raad.papendrecht.nl/Documenten/D03-20251002-RIB-Vaststelling-Water-en-rioleringsprogramma-2025-2029-met-bijlage.pdf inventories municipal pumping assets and statutory wastewater/rainwater/groundwater duties.

A strategy statement that current climate vulnerability is comparatively limited is not a safe-state observation and does not validate any simulated event magnitude. Buitendijkse direct-river exposure and binnendijkse breach/pluvial pathways require separate geometries and consequences.

Plans and inventories are static/design evidence, not current rainfall, sewer/singel/groundwater/pump condition, river boundary, completed measure or event depth. No blanket machine-reuse licence was identified.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Alblasserwaard peil system and crisis plan for water nuisance/regional barriers
evidenceSources.edition: Peilbesluit adopted 9 October 2023; crisis plan PB-CZO-001 version 5.0 and current pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The authority defines the 24,000-ha Alblasserwaard as low polders with fine watercourses and higher boezem systems, bounded by the Lek, Noord, Beneden/Boven-Merwede, Zouweboezem and Merwedekanaal; major settlement/work concentrations include Papendrecht.

The crisis plan at https://www.waterschaprivierenland.nl/_flysystem/media/pb-czo-001-v5.0-cbp-wateroverlast-en-regionale-keringen.pdf lists electrically driven Papendrecht Hoog pump at 1 x 9 m³/min with no alternative coupling and provides 48–12-hour and 12–0-hour rainfall-alert/action procedures.

The peil decision uses a desired groundwater/surface-water regime and records control objectives; the crisis plan exposes decision timing and dependencies. Neither is an event observation, selected breach, pump status or proof of available staff/material.
The published PDF is public governance/technical context; exact redistribution terms were not identified. Version/date, stale technical appendix dates and authority ownership must remain explicit.

supports: The bounded query returns two primary and zero regional candidates: Noord km 977.7 (dkr16 AW112) and Beneden Merwede km 971.4 (dkr16 AW080).

Point-in-polygon against the generated generalized boundary contains the Noord candidate; the Beneden-Merwede candidate lies within the query envelope but outside. Both remain hydrologically relevant neighbouring case choices subject to authority review.
Candidate points, water/dike-ring ids and frequency flags are scenario-selection metadata, not active failures, forecasts, connected footprints, metre depths, arrival or safe-state evidence.
LIWO release/licence, geometry, scenario metadata and authority approval must remain attached; administrative containment cannot select an incident automatically.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Current N3/Baanhoek bridge closure, temporary ferries, road/transit and external-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal page last changed 1 June 2026; measures valid 17 July 2026–21 April 2027; NWB-Light 1 August 2026; GTFS v9543 valid 30 August–12 December 2026; RIVM acute care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: Rijkswaterstaat closes the N3 Papendrecht bridge fully to road traffic for nine months. The Baanhoek bridge cycle path is also closed except for emergency services and specified target transport; two temporary passenger ferries connect Papendrecht and Dordrecht.

Local traffic/parking measures are explicitly valid 17 July 2026 through 21 April 2027. This current valid-time closure contradicts treating the N3 as ordinary 150-unit scenario capacity; ferry schedules do not establish incident-time sailing, queue or emergency throughput.
The graph has five edges: three A15 edges sharing one physical corridor, N214 and N3. No ProRail station lies inside; 34 GTFS stop areas are schedule context. NWB is CC0.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 is CC0 and has no respondent point inside GM0590. Approximate centre distances are Albert Schweitzer Dordrecht 4.77 km, Maasstad 12.92 km and IJsselland 15.42 km; distance is not route time, ambulance state or acceptance.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Oosteind/Noordhoek/Slobbengors industry, waterways and dangerous-goods routes
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal freight page and 2025 budget/Omgevingsvisie public evidence inspected 3 September 2026; CBS statistics 2025
supports: Papendrecht designates the N214 and Burgemeester Keijzerweg sections toward N3/Oosteind for dangerous-goods transport and requires exemption outside designated routes. This is corridor eligibility, not an incident.

Municipal policy identifies Oosteind on the Merwede/inlet harbours as its largest important water-linked industrial site, alongside water-linked Noordhoek and the Slobbengors aerospace/Fokker complex; the Kooyhaven has inland-shipping facilities and Port of Rotterdam nautical management.

CBS assigns Bedrijventerrein Oosteind en Ketel only 25 residents but 220 businesses and 221 non-residential buildings. Resident weighting cannot represent workers, freight, vessel, contractor or shift populations.

Industrial identity, dangerous-goods route and harbour use do not prove current substance inventory, source term, site/vessel state, plume, workforce or protective action. Missing REV/operator data remains Unknown, not safe.

residualLimitations: This artifact audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a forecast, warning, evacuation instruction, hydraulic assessment, bridge/ferry decision, hospital status or operator restoration commitment.

CBS 2025 rows are rounded/suppressed and residents exclude industrial/aerospace workers, freight/vessel/ferry users, pupils, patients/staff, responders and displaced people; no timestamped dynamic occupancy is consumed.

The N3 closure is current and authoritative for its validity period; temporary ferry timetables and permissions still do not establish incident-time sailing, queue, accessibility or emergency throughput.
A15 series edges are not additive. NWB/GTFS geometry and schedules do not establish actual operation, passengers, bridge condition or alternatives.
Zero internal RIVM acute-care respondent points does not erase care demand; centre distance is not route time, ambulance availability, acceptance, beds, staff, utilities or backup.
Industrial identities, harbour use and dangerous-goods routes do not establish substances, source term, plume, workforce, vessel state or protective action; absent REV/operator data is Unknown.
One Stedin sample with null capacity values, 54 antennas and 21 schools are planning/register context, not connectivity, load, signal, occupancy, shelter, backup or repair.
Canonical wildfire has zero local flame but remote smoke; this is not proof of zero local ignition risk and lacks a selected source/perimeter/plume.

Complete physical electricity, gas, drinking-water, wastewater, telecom, care, supply and emergency-resource topology/live state may be unavailable or security-sensitive and remains Unknown or explicitly synthetic.

Exact hazard, neighbourhood, affected-population, service, recovery and person-hour values remain synthetic screening until critical/high findings are corrected and authorities review the selected event; impacts beyond T+72 are outside scope.
